sanskrit: prasūtyante prasūtyante kanyaiva tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi sa tvaṃ dadasva māṃ rājñe pratigṛhya hayottamān
english: After each birth, after each birth, you shall become a maiden again. Therefore give me to the king, having first received those finest horses.

sanskrit: nṛpebhyo hi caturbhyas te pūrṇāny aṣṭau śatāni vai bhaviṣyanti tathā putrā mama catvāra eva ca
english: From four kings there will indeed be eight full hundreds of horses for you, and four sons for me.

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ mama saṃhāro gurvarthaṃ dvijasattama eṣā tāvan mama prajñā yathā vā manyase dvija
english: Let my deliverance be accomplished for the sake of my teacher, O best of twice-born. This is my judgment for now — or think as you see fit, O brahmin.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sa muniḥ kanyayā gālavas tadā haryaśvaṃ pṛthivīpālam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the maiden, the sage Gālava then spoke these words to Haryaśva, guardian of the earth.

sanskrit: iyaṃ kanyā naraśreṣṭha haryaśva pratigṛhyatām caturbhāgena śulkasya janayasvaikam ātmajam
english: O best of men, O Haryaśva, accept this maiden. In exchange for a quarter of the bride-price, beget one son upon her.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya sa tāṃ kanyāṃ gālavaṃ pratinandya ca samaye deśakāle ca labdhavān sutam īpsitam
english: He accepted that maiden, praised Gālava joyfully, and at the proper time and place obtained the desired son.

sanskrit: tato vasumanā nāma vasubhyo vasumattaraḥ vasuprakhyo narapatiḥ sa babhūva vasupradaḥ
english: Then there was born a king named Vasumanas, richer than the wealthy, comparable to wealth itself, a bestower of wealth.

sanskrit: atha kāle punar dhīmān gālavaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ upasaṃgamya covāca haryaśvaṃ prītimānasam
english: Then in due time the wise Gālava came back again and, approaching Haryaśva with a glad heart, spoke to him.

sanskrit: jāto nṛpa sutas te 'yaṃ bālabhāskarasaṃnibhaḥ kālo gantuṃ naraśreṣṭha bhikṣārtham aparaṃ nṛpam
english: O king, your son has been born, blazing like the infant sun. The time has come, O best of men, to go to another king for the rest of the gift.

sanskrit: haryaśvaḥ satyavacane sthitaḥ sthitvā ca pauruṣe durlabhatvād dhayānāṃ ca pradadau mādhavīṃ punaḥ
english: Haryaśva, firm in his word and steadfast in his manly duty, and knowing the rarity of such horses, gave Mādhavī back again.

sanskrit: mādhavī ca punar dīptāṃ parityajya nṛpaśriyam kumārī kāmato bhūtvā gālavaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvagāt
english: And Mādhavī, renouncing the splendid royal majesty once more, willingly became a virgin again and followed behind Gālava.

sanskrit: tvayy eva tāvat tiṣṭhantu hayā ity uktavān dvijaḥ prayayau kanyayā sārdhaṃ divodāsaṃ prajeśvaram
english: "Let the horses remain with you for now," said the brahmin, and he departed with the maiden toward Divodāsa, lord of his people.

sanskrit: gālava uvāca mahāvīryo mahīpālaḥ kāśīnām īśvaraḥ prabhuḥ divodāsa iti khyāto bhaimasenir narādhipaḥ
english: Gālava said: There is a king of mighty valor, guardian of the earth, lord and master of the Kāśis, known as Divodāsa, son of Bhīmasena, ruler of men.

sanskrit: tatra gacchāvahe bhadre śanair āgaccha mā śucaḥ dhārmikaḥ saṃyame yuktaḥ satyaś caiva janeśvaraḥ
english: Let us go there, dear one. Come along gently; do not grieve. He is righteous, devoted to self-restraint, and truthful — that lord of his people.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tam upāgamya sa munir nyāyatas tena satkṛtaḥ gālavaḥ prasavasyārthe taṃ nṛpaṃ pratyacodayat
english: Nārada said: The sage approached him and was duly honored by him. Then Gālava urged that king for the purpose of procreating.

sanskrit: divodāsa uvāca śrutam etan mayā pūrvaṃ kim uktvā vistaraṃ dvija kāṅkṣito hi mayaiṣo 'rthaḥ śrutvaitad dvijasattama
english: Divodāsa said: I have heard all of this before — why speak at length, O brahmin? This very matter has indeed been desired by me upon hearing it, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: etac ca me bahumataṃ yad utsṛjya narādhipān mām evam upayāto 'si bhāvi caitad asaṃśayam
english: And this is highly agreeable to me: that passing over other kings you have come to me in this way. Without doubt, this outcome was destined.

sanskrit: sa eva vibhavo 'smākam aśvānām api gālava aham apy ekam evāsyāṃ janayiṣyāmi pārthivam
english: The same wealth of horses is ours as well, O Gālava. I too shall beget only one royal son upon her.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tathety uktvā dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ prādāt kanyāṃ mahīpateḥ vidhipūrvaṃ ca tāṃ rājā kanyāṃ pratigṛhītavān
english: Nārada said: Saying "so be it," the best of brahmins gave the maiden to the lord of the earth, and the king received that maiden according to proper rite.

sanskrit: reme sa tasyāṃ rājarṣiḥ prabhāvatyāṃ yathā raviḥ svāhāyāṃ ca yathā vahnir yathā śacyāṃ sa vāsavaḥ
english: That royal sage sported with her radiantly as the sun sports with his consort, as Fire sports with Svāhā, as Vāsava sports with Śacī.

sanskrit: yathā candraś ca rohiṇyāṃ yathā dhūmorṇayā yamaḥ varuṇaś ca yathā gauryāṃ yathā carddhyāṃ dhaneśvaraḥ
english: As the Moon with Rohiṇī, as Yama with Dhumorna, as Varuṇa with Gaurī, as the lord of wealth with his prosperity.

sanskrit: yathā nārāyaṇo lakṣmyāṃ jāhnavyāṃ ca yathodadhiḥ yathā rudraś ca rudrāṇyāṃ yathā vedyāṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: As Nārāyaṇa with Lakṣmī, as the ocean with the Jāhnavī, as Rudra with Rudrani, as the Grandfather with the sacrificial altar-Goddess.

sanskrit: adṛśyantyāṃ ca vāsiṣṭho vasiṣṭhaś cākṣamālayā cyavanaś ca sukanyāyāṃ pulastyaḥ saṃdhyayā yathā
english: As Vasiṣṭha with Adrishyanti, and Vasiṣṭha also with Akshamala, as Cyavana with Sukanyā, as Pulastya with Sandhya.

sanskrit: agastyaś cāpi vaidarbhyāṃ sāvitryāṃ satyavān yathā yathā bhṛguḥ pulomāyām adityāṃ kaśyapo yathā
english: As Agastya with the maiden of Vidarbha, as Satyavān with Sāvitrī, as Bhṛgu with Pulomā, as Kaśyapa with Aditi.

sanskrit: reṇukāyāṃ yathārcīko haimavatyāṃ ca kauśikaḥ bṛhaspatiś ca tārāyāṃ śukraś ca śataparvayā
english: As Richika with Reṇukā, as Kauśika with the daughter of the Himālaya, as Bṛhaspati with Tārā, as Śukra with Shataparvā.

sanskrit: yathā bhūmyāṃ bhūmipatir urvaśyāṃ ca purūravāḥ ṛcīkaḥ satyavatyāṃ ca sarasvatyāṃ yathā manuḥ
english: As the lord of earth with the Earth-Goddess, as Purūravas with Urvaśī, as Richika with Satyavatī, as Manu with Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: tathā tu ramamāṇasya divodāsasya bhūpateḥ mādhavī janayām āsa putram ekaṃ pratardanam
english: Thus while King Divodāsa sported with her, Mādhavī gave birth to a single son named Pratardana.

sanskrit: athājagāma bhagavān divodāsaṃ sa gālavaḥ samaye samanuprāpte vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then the blessed Gālava came to Divodāsa when the appointed time had arrived and spoke these words.

sanskrit: niryātayatu me kanyāṃ bhavāṃs tiṣṭhantu vājinaḥ yāvad anyatra gacchāmi śulkārthaṃ pṛthivīpate
english: "Let your lordship return the maiden to me; let the horses remain with you while I go elsewhere for the bride-price, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: divodāso 'tha dharmātmā samaye gālavasya tām kanyāṃ niryātayām āsa sthitaḥ satye mahīpatiḥ
english: Then Divodāsa, righteous in soul, at Gālava's appointed time, returned that maiden — that king standing firm in his truth.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca tathaiva sā śriyaṃ tyaktvā kanyā bhūtvā yaśasvinī mādhavī gālavaṃ vipram anvayāt satyasaṃgarā
english: Nārada said: Just as before, she renounced her royal splendor and became a maiden again — the glorious Mādhavī, true to her vow, followed the brahmin Gālava.

sanskrit: gālavo vimṛśann eva svakāryagatamānasaḥ jagāma bhojanagaraṃ draṣṭum auśīnaraṃ nṛpam
english: Gālava, reflecting and with his mind fixed on his purpose, went to the city of the Bhojas to see the king Uśīnara.

sanskrit: tam uvācātha gatvā sa nṛpatiṃ satyavikramam iyaṃ kanyā sutau dvau te janayiṣyati pārthivau
english: Going to that king of true valor, he said: "This maiden will bear you two royal sons."

sanskrit: asyāṃ bhavān avāptārtho bhavitā pretya ceha ca somārkapratisaṃkāśau janayitvā sutau nṛpa
english: "Begetting two sons equal to the Moon and Sun upon her, you shall gain your object both in this world and the next, O king."

sanskrit: śulkaṃ tu sarvadharmajña hayānāṃ candravarcasām ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ deyaṃ mahyaṃ catuḥśatam
english: "But the bride-price to be paid to me, O knower of all dharma, is four hundred horses of moon-like splendor, each with one black ear."

sanskrit: gurvartho 'yaṃ samārambho na hayaiḥ kṛtyam asti me yadi śakyaṃ mahārāja kriyatāṃ mā vicāryatām
english: "This undertaking is for the sake of my teacher; I have no personal use for the horses. If it is possible, O great king, let it be done without hesitation."

sanskrit: anapatyo 'si rājarṣe putrau janaya pārthiva pitṝn putraplavena tvam ātmānaṃ caiva tāraya
english: "You are without a son, O royal sage. Beget sons, O king; ferry your ancestors and yourself across by the raft of sons."

sanskrit: na putraphalabhoktā hi rājarṣe pātyate divaḥ na yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ yatra gacchanty anātmajāḥ
english: "For he who enjoys the fruit of having sons, O royal sage, does not fall from heaven; he does not go to the terrible hell where the sonless go."

sanskrit: etac cānyac ca vividhaṃ śrutvā gālavabhāṣitam uśīnaraḥ prativaco dadau tasya narādhipaḥ
english: Having heard all this and much else besides from Gālava's speech, Uśīnara the king of men gave him his reply.

sanskrit: śrutavān asmi te vākyaṃ yathā vadasi gālava vidhis tu balavān brahman pravaṇaṃ hi mano mama
english: Uśīnara said: I have heard your words as you have spoken them, O Gālava. Fate is powerful, O brahmin — my mind is indeed inclined toward this.

sanskrit: śate dve tu mamāśvānām īdṛśānāṃ dvijottama itareṣāṃ sahasrāṇi subahūni caranti me
english: "Of horses like these I have two hundred, O best of twice-born. Thousands upon thousands of others roam in my possession."

sanskrit: aham apy ekam evāsyāṃ janayiṣyāmi gālava putraṃ dvija gataṃ mārgaṃ gamiṣyāmi parair aham
english: "I too shall beget only one son upon her, O Gālava, O brahmin. I shall travel the path that others have gone."

sanskrit: mūlyenāpi samaṃ kuryāṃ tavāhaṃ dvijasattama paurajānapadārthaṃ tu mamārtho nātmabhogataḥ
english: "I could even make up the full price for you, O best of twice-born — but my wealth belongs to my townspeople and country folk, not for my own enjoyment."

sanskrit: kāmato hi dhanaṃ rājā pārakyaṃ yaḥ prayacchati na sa dharmeṇa dharmātman yujyate yaśasā na ca
english: "For a king who gives away others' wealth out of desire, O righteous one, is not associated with virtue or with glory."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ pratigrahīṣyāmi dadātv etāṃ bhavān mama kumārīṃ devagarbhābhām ekaputrabhavāya me
english: "So I will accept her — let your lordship give me this maiden, radiant as a goddess, to beget one son upon her."

sanskrit: tathā tu bahukalyāṇam uktavantaṃ narādhipam uśīnaraṃ dvijaśreṣṭho gālavaḥ pratyapūjayat
english: The best of brahmins, Gālava, honored King Uśīnara in return for speaking so auspiciously in so many ways.

sanskrit: uśīnaraṃ pratigrāhya gālavaḥ prayayau vanam reme sa tāṃ samāsādya kṛtapuṇya iva śriyam
english: Having given her over to Uśīnara, Gālava departed to the forest. Uśīnara sported with her, who had come to him, like one who has earned good merit delighting in prosperity.

sanskrit: kandareṣu ca śailānāṃ nadīnāṃ nirjhareṣu ca udyāneṣu vicitreṣu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca
english: In the gorges of mountains and the cascades of rivers, in pleasure-gardens of all kinds, in forests and groves,

sanskrit: harmyeṣu ramaṇīyeṣu prāsādaśikhareṣu ca vātāyanavimāneṣu tathā garbhagṛheṣu ca
english: In delightful mansions and on the pinnacles of palaces, in airy upper-chambers and in inner apartments,

sanskrit: tato 'sya samaye jajñe putro bālaraviprabhaḥ śibir nāmnābhivikhyāto yaḥ sa pārthivasattamaḥ
english: Then in due time there was born to him a son blazing like the young sun — he who became widely renowned as Śibi, that best of kings.

sanskrit: upasthāya sa taṃ vipro gālavaḥ pratigṛhya ca kanyāṃ prayātas tāṃ rājan dṛṣṭavān vinatātmajam
english: The brahmin Gālava came to him, received the maiden back, and as he departed, O king, he saw the son of Vinatā.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca gālavaṃ vainateyo 'tha prahasann idam abravīt diṣṭyā kṛtārthaṃ paśyāmi bhavantam iha vai dvija
english: Nārada said: The son of Vinatā then laughingly said to Gālava: "By good fortune I see you here with your purpose accomplished, O brahmin."

sanskrit: gālavas tu vacaḥ śrutvā vainateyena bhāṣitam caturbhāgāvaśiṣṭaṃ tad ācakhyau kāryam asya hi
english: Gālava, hearing the words spoken by the son of Vinatā, reported to him that a quarter of his task still remained undone.

sanskrit: suparṇas tv abravīd enaṃ gālavaṃ patatāṃ varaḥ prayatnas te na kartavyo naiṣa saṃpatsyate tava
english: Suparṇa, best among birds, said to him: "No effort need be made by you — this will not succeed for you."

sanskrit: purā hi kanyakubje vai gādheḥ satyavatīṃ sutām bhāryārthe 'varayat kanyām ṛcīkas tena bhāṣitaḥ
english: "For long ago, at Kanyakubja, Richika chose the maiden Satyavatī, daughter of Gādhi, as his wife, and being spoken to said:"

sanskrit: ekataḥśyāmakarṇānāṃ hayānāṃ candravarcasām bhagavan dīyatāṃ mahyaṃ sahasram iti gālava
english: "'Let a thousand horses of moon-like splendor, each with one black ear, be given to me, O lord' — so spoke he, O Gālava."

sanskrit: ṛcīkas tu tathety uktvā varuṇasyālayaṃ gataḥ aśvatīrthe hayāṃl labdhvā dattavān pārthivāya vai
english: "Richika, saying 'so be it,' went to the abode of Varuṇa, obtained the horses at the Ashvatirtha ford, and gave them to the king."

sanskrit: iṣṭvā te puṇḍarīkeṇa dattā rājñā dvijātiṣu tebhyo dve dve śate krītvā prāptās te pārthivais tadā
english: "Those horses were given away by the king to brahmins after a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice. Two hundred each were then bought from them by kings."

sanskrit: aparāṇy api catvāri śatāni dvijasattama nīyamānāni saṃtāre hṛtāny āsan vitastayā evaṃ na śakyam aprāpyaṃ prāptuṃ gālava karhi cit
english: "The remaining four hundred, O best of twice-born, were swept away by the Vitastā river while being ferried across. Thus the unattainable can never be attained, O Gālava."

sanskrit: imām aśvaśatābhyāṃ vai dvābhyāṃ tasmai nivedaya viśvāmitrāya dharmātman ṣaḍbhir aśvaśataiḥ saha tato 'si gatasaṃmohaḥ kṛtakṛtyo dvijarṣabha
english: "Present this maiden along with these two hundred horses to Viśvāmitra, O righteous one — six hundred horses in all. Then you shall be free of your confusion, your duty done, O bull among twice-born."

sanskrit: gālavas taṃ tathety uktvā suparṇasahitas tataḥ ādāyāśvāṃś ca kanyāṃ ca viśvāmitram upāgamat
english: Gālava said "so be it" to him, and then together with Suparṇa, taking the horses and the maiden, he came to Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: gālava uvāca aśvānāṃ kāṅkṣitārthānāṃ ṣaḍ imāni śatāni vai śatadvayena kanyeyaṃ bhavatā pratigṛhyatām
english: Gālava said: Here are six hundred of the desired horses. Together with the remaining two hundred, accept this maiden, your lordship.

sanskrit: asyāṃ rājarṣibhiḥ putrā jātā vai dhārmikās trayaḥ caturthaṃ janayatv ekaṃ bhavān api narottama
english: "By royal sages three righteous sons have already been born upon her. Let your lordship also beget a fourth single one, O best of men."

sanskrit: pūrṇāny evaṃ śatāny aṣṭau turagāṇāṃ bhavantu te bhavato hy anṛṇo bhūtvā tapaḥ kuryāṃ yathāsukham
english: "In this way eight full hundreds of horses will be yours. Being freed from your debt to me, I shall then practice austerities at my ease."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca viśvāmitras tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā gālavaṃ saha pakṣiṇā kanyāṃ ca tāṃ varārohām idam ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: Nārada said: Viśvāmitra, seeing Gālava along with the bird and that woman of finest form, spoke these words.

sanskrit: kim iyaṃ pūrvam eveha na dattā mama gālava putrā mamaiva catvāro bhaveyuḥ kulabhāvanāḥ
english: "Why was this maiden not given to me here at the very beginning, O Gālava? All four sons could have been mine, nurturing the lineage."

sanskrit: pratigṛhṇāmi te kanyām ekaputraphalāya vai aśvāś cāśramam āsādya tiṣṭhantu mama sarvaśaḥ
english: "I accept your maiden for the fruit of one son. And let the horses all go to my hermitage and remain there."

sanskrit: sa tayā ramamāṇo 'tha viśvāmitro mahādyutiḥ ātmajaṃ janayām āsa mādhavīputram aṣṭakam
english: Then the great-splendored Viśvāmitra, sporting with her, begat a son — Aṣṭaka, born of Mādhavī.

sanskrit: jātamātraṃ sutaṃ taṃ ca viśvāmitro mahādyutiḥ saṃyojyārthais tathā dharmair aśvais taiḥ samayojayat
english: As soon as that son was born, the great-splendored Viśvāmitra invested him with wealth, with duties, and with those very horses.

sanskrit: athāṣṭakaḥ puraṃ prāyāt tadā somapuraprabham niryātya kanyāṃ śiṣyāya kauśiko 'pi vanaṃ yayau
english: Then Aṣṭaka went to his city, which shone like the city of the Moon, while Kauśika, after giving the maiden to his disciple, went to the forest.

sanskrit: gālavo 'pi suparṇena saha niryātya dakṣiṇām manasābhipratītena kanyām idam uvāca ha
english: Gālava too, setting out southward together with Suparṇa, his mind at peace, said this to the maiden.

sanskrit: jāto dānapatiḥ putras tvayā śūras tathāparaḥ satyadharmarataś cānyo yajvā cāpi tathāparaḥ
english: "A son who is a lord of giving has been born of you, and another who is a hero, yet another devoted to truth and dharma, and likewise one who is a great sacrificer."

sanskrit: tad āgaccha varārohe tāritas te pitā sutaiḥ catvāraś caiva rājānas tathāhaṃ ca sumadhyame
english: "Therefore come, O fine-hipped one — your father has been ferried across by his sons, and four kings as well, and I too, O slender-waisted one."

sanskrit: gālavas tv abhyanujñāya suparṇaṃ pannagāśanam pitur niryātya tāṃ kanyāṃ prayayau vanam eva ha
english: Gālava took leave of Suparṇa, devourer of serpents, delivered the maiden to her father, and then departed to the forest.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sa tu rājā punas tasyāḥ kartukāmaḥ svayaṃvaram upagamyāśramapadaṃ gaṅgāyamunasaṃgame
english: Nārada said: But the king, wishing to hold a svayamvara for her again, came to the hermitage at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

sanskrit: gṛhītamālyadāmāṃ tāṃ ratham āropya mādhavīm pūrur yaduś ca bhaginīm āśrame paryadhāvatām
english: Placing Mādhavī, garland-wreath in hand, upon a chariot, Pūru and Yadu ran around their sister in the hermitage.

sanskrit: nāgayakṣamanuṣyāṇāṃ patatrimṛgapakṣiṇām śailadrumavanaukānām āsīt tatra samāgamaḥ
english: There was a great gathering there of serpents, yakshas, and humans, of flying creatures, beasts, and birds, of those dwelling in mountains, trees, and forests.

sanskrit: nānāpuruṣadeśānām īśvaraiś ca samākulam ṛṣibhir brahmakalpaiś ca samantād āvṛtaṃ vanam
english: The forest was crowded with lords of many human realms and surrounded on all sides by sages equal to Brahmā.

sanskrit: nirdiśyamāneṣu tu sā vareṣu varavarṇinī varān utkramya sarvāṃs tān vanaṃ vṛtavatī varam
english: But when the suitors were being named, she of finest complexion passed over all of them and chose the forest as her mate.

sanskrit: avatīrya rathāt kanyā namaskṛtvā ca bandhuṣu upagamya vanaṃ puṇyaṃ tapas tepe yayātijā
english: Descending from the chariot, the maiden paid obeisance to her kinsmen, and entering the sacred forest, that daughter of Yayāti performed austerities.
